title: Introducing AG-UI: The Protocol Where Agents Meet Users
summary: CopilotKit announced AG-UI, an open Agent-User Interaction Protocol in which a client sends one POST to an agent endpoint and then receives a single stream of JSON events over HTTP (or an optional binary channel). The event set covers text messages, tool-call starts, state deltas and lifecycle signals, with TypeScript and Python SDKs. CopilotKit positions it as a way to normalise the differing conventions of frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra and AG2.
relevance: Defines a framework-neutral event and shared-state stream between agent and user, a candidate carrier for task state and human approval when work moves between agent backends.
search_query: CopilotKit AG-UI protocol launch agent user interaction

title: Microsoft releases .NET SDK for AG-UI agent-user interaction protocol
summary: InfoWorld reports that Microsoft, working with CopilotKit, released a .NET SDK for AG-UI (announced 25 September 2026), hosted in the AG-UI repository next to the TypeScript and Python SDKs and published on NuGet under MIT. It ships five packages, including AGUI.Server to expose an agent as an AG-UI endpoint and AGUI.Client to consume one, and the event set now includes subagent and activity-progress events. Microsoft Agent Framework's .NET AG-UI support is now built on this SDK.
relevance: Shows AG-UI becoming a multi-language, multi-vendor interface, so an agent front end can stay the same while the backend framework or runtime changes.

title: Introducing A2UI: An open project for agent-driven interfaces
summary: Google released A2UI v0.8, an Apache-2.0 project in which agents describe user interfaces as declarative data rather than executable code, and the host renders them with its own native widget catalogue. Launch renderers cover Flutter, Web Components/Lit and Angular. Google says A2UI payloads can travel over A2A, that AG-UI/CopilotKit had day-zero compatibility, and that Gemini Enterprise and Flutter's GenUI SDK use it.
relevance: Lets a remote (possibly cross-organisation) agent in a delegation chain request user input without shipping code into the host, which matters for safety when tasks are handed between agents.

title: MCP Apps - Bringing UI Capabilities To MCP Clients
summary: The MCP maintainers announced MCP Apps as the first official MCP extension, first proposed in November 2025. It builds on MCP-UI and the OpenAI Apps SDK. Tools can link to ui:// resources that render interactive interfaces inside the conversation, with Claude, Goose, VS Code Insiders and ChatGPT listed as supporting clients. The security model combines sandboxed iframes, host review of HTML, loggable JSON-RPC between the UI and the host, and optional user approval for tool calls initiated from the UI.
relevance: Standardises agent-to-user UI on the tool layer across hosts, with explicit human-approval and audit hooks that portable tasks can rely on.
search_query: MCP Apps official extension announcement OpenAI Anthropic interactive UI

title: OpenAI Expands ChatGPT with Embedded Apps and Developer SDK
summary: At DevDay 2025 OpenAI launched apps inside ChatGPT, with partners such as Booking.com, Coursera, Figma, Zillow and Spotify, and a preview Apps SDK built on MCP that lets third parties render interactive UIs and connect external data. Users can sign in to existing accounts, and OpenAI said Instant Checkout would let developers charge inside ChatGPT. The article notes open questions about how much conversation context apps can see and how app ranking will be governed.
relevance: Third-party services now act inside a single agent surface on behalf of users, which raises questions about context sharing and who governs the hand-off.

title: Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
summary: Google announced AP2, an open, payment-method-agnostic protocol that can be used as an extension of A2A and MCP. Users' instructions are captured as cryptographically signed Mandates backed by verifiable credentials: an Intent Mandate for pre-authorised rules and a Cart Mandate for the exact approved items and price. Google says this gives a non-repudiable audit trail. It lists more than 60 collaborators, including Adyen, American Express, Coinbase, Mastercard, PayPal and Salesforce, and released an A2A x402 extension for stablecoin payments.
relevance: Provides a signed, portable record of delegated user authority that can travel with a task across agents and organisations, which is central to accountable delegation.

title: Stripe powers Instant Checkout in ChatGPT and releases Agentic Commerce Protocol codeveloped with OpenAI
summary: Stripe announced that it powers Instant Checkout in ChatGPT and released the Agentic Commerce Protocol, an open standard co-developed with OpenAI that lets merchants sell through any AI agent while keeping control of catalogue, branding and fulfilment. A new Shared Payment Token lets the agent start a payment without seeing the buyer's credentials, and each token is scoped to one merchant and one cart. US ChatGPT users could buy from US Etsy sellers at launch, and Shopify merchants were described as coming soon.
relevance: A scoped, single-use credential passed from agent to merchant is a concrete pattern for least-privilege hand-off of authority across organisations.

title: Visa Introduces Trusted Agent Protocol: An Ecosystem-Led Framework for AI Commerce
summary: Visa, together with Cloudflare, released the Trusted Agent Protocol. It builds on HTTP Message Signatures and aligns with the IETF Web Bot Auth work, so approved AI agents can cryptographically signal agent intent, consumer recognition and, optionally, payment information to merchants. Early partners include Adyen, Checkout.com, Coinbase, Fiserv, Microsoft, Shopify, Stripe and Worldpay. Visa says it will complement ACP, work with Coinbase on x402 interoperability, and pursue alignment with IETF, OpenID Foundation and EMVCo. It also cites a rise of more than 4,700% in AI-driven traffic to US retail sites.
relevance: Gives merchants a way to verify which agent is acting for which consumer when a task crosses an organisational boundary.
search_query: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol Cloudflare announcement

title: Mastercard unveils Agent Pay, pioneering agentic payments technology to power commerce in the age of AI
summary: Mastercard launched Agent Pay, built around Agentic Tokens that extend its existing tokenisation (card-on-file, contactless, Payment Passkeys). Agents must be registered and verified before they can pay, consumers can set spending limits, and merchants and issuers can identify agent-initiated transactions. Mastercard named Microsoft, IBM watsonx Orchestrate, Braintree and Checkout.com as collaborators and said it would explore applying the Model Context Protocol to Secure Remote Commerce.
relevance: Binds a delegated payment credential to a registered agent identity with user-set limits, an early network-level pattern for accountable delegation.
search_query: Mastercard Agent Pay launch agentic tokens announcement

title: Launching the x402 Foundation with Coinbase, and support for x402 transactions
summary: Cloudflare announced it would form the x402 Foundation with Coinbase to steward x402, the protocol that revives HTTP 402 Payment Required for machine-to-machine payments. Cloudflare added x402 support to its Agents SDK and to MCP servers, so paid tools can be exposed with an optional confirmation step for the client before it pays. It also proposed a 'deferred' scheme that separates the cryptographic handshake from settlement, so charges can be batched, for example in pay-per-crawl.
relevance: Moves agent-to-tool payment into a neutral governance body and the MCP layer, so tasks can pay for resources across organisations without bespoke billing integrations.
notes: Author taken from the page's author card; publication date from page metadata.

title: Under the Hood: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
summary: Google introduced UCP, an open-source agentic-commerce standard co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target and Walmart and endorsed by more than 20 others, including Visa, Mastercard, Stripe and American Express. Businesses publish a JSON manifest at /.well-known/ucp that declares services, capabilities and payment handlers, and they can integrate via REST APIs, A2A or MCP. UCP works with AP2 for payments, and the merchant remains Merchant of Record.
relevance: A well-known capability manifest lets any agent discover and act on a merchant across organisational lines, with transport bindings to A2A and MCP.

title: Agentic Browser Security: Indirect Prompt Injection in Perplexity Comet
summary: Brave disclosed that Perplexity's Comet browser passed webpage content to its LLM without separating it from user instructions. In a demonstration, a hidden Reddit comment made the agent read the user's Perplexity email and a Gmail one-time password and exfiltrate them, which enabled account takeover without further user input. Brave reported the flaw on 25 July 2025, found Perplexity's fixes incomplete, and recommended isolating agentic browsing, checking that actions match the user's intent, and requiring explicit confirmation for sensitive actions.
relevance: Shows that an agent acting with a user's full authenticated privileges across sites breaks same-origin assumptions, so delegated cross-organisation actions need confirmation and isolation.
search_query: Brave Comet indirect prompt injection disclosure agentic browser

title: Piloting Claude in Chrome
summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of a Chrome-extension browser agent to 1,000 Max-plan users. In red-teaming of 123 cases across 29 attack scenarios, Anthropic reports that the attack success rate fell from 23.6% to 11.2% with new mitigations, and from 35.7% to 0% on a four-type browser-specific challenge set. Users grant or revoke access per site, Claude asks for confirmation before high-risk actions such as purchasing or publishing, and some site categories are blocked. Later updates widened availability (Max beta in November 2025; Pro/Team/Enterprise in December 2025).
relevance: Gives quantified evidence that human-in-the-loop confirmation and per-site permissions are still needed when an agent acts on third-party sites.

title: Perplexity is using stealth, undeclared crawlers to evade website no-crawl directives
summary: Cloudflare reported that when its declared PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User agents were blocked, Perplexity appeared to fall back to an undeclared crawler. Cloudflare says this crawler used a generic Chrome-on-macOS user agent and rotated IPs and ASNs outside Perplexity's published ranges, across tens of thousands of domains. Cloudflare de-listed Perplexity as a verified bot and added blocking signatures. It contrasted this with OpenAI's ChatGPT Agent, which it says signs requests with Web Bot Auth. Perplexity disputed the findings.
relevance: Shows the dispute over whether a user-directed agent must identify itself to the sites it acts on, which motivated signed-agent schemes.

title: Amazon sues Perplexity over covert AI agent access to marketplace
summary: Amazon filed suit against Perplexity on 4 November 2025 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California (case 3:25-cv-09514). The suit alleges that Comet's shopping agent violated the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act and California's computer-fraud statute by using customers' accounts while sending a Google Chrome user-agent string that disguised agent activity as human browsing. Perplexity responded the same day with a blog post titled 'Bullying is Not Innovation'.
relevance: First major lawsuit over whether a platform can refuse an agent acting on a user's behalf, which bears directly on the legitimacy of cross-organisation delegation.
search_query: Amazon sues Perplexity Comet agentic shopping lawsuit
notes: Claims are Amazon's allegations, not findings. Reuters/Bloomberg originals not fetched.

title: Court blocks Perplexity's Comet browser from Amazon's accounts
summary: On 9 March 2026, Judge Maxine M. Chesney (N.D. Cal., 25-cv-09514-MMC) granted Amazon a preliminary injunction barring Perplexity from using Comet agents to access password-protected Amazon accounts. The court found Amazon likely to succeed under the CFAA and California Penal Code s. 502 because access occurred with the user's permission but without Amazon's authorisation. The order was stayed seven days to allow an appeal, Perplexity was ordered to destroy collected customer data, and no bond was required.
relevance: A court treated user consent as insufficient without the platform's authorisation, which constrains delegated agent actions across organisations.

title: US court overturns Amazon injunction against Perplexity AI
summary: A three-judge Ninth Circuit panel vacated the March 2026 preliminary injunction against Perplexity's Comet browser. The panel found Amazon unlikely to succeed on its CFAA and California claims because, on the current record, Perplexity itself did not access Amazon's systems and the assistant acted as a tool on the user's instructions. The panel said the ruling is limited to the existing record and sets no broad rule on agentic AI. The case returns to the district court.
relevance: An appellate court treated a user-directed agent as the user's tool, an open legal question for accountability when agents act across organisational boundaries.

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Atlas Browser With Built-In Agent Mode
summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas, a macOS browser with ChatGPT built in, with Windows and mobile versions to follow. Its agent mode, limited to Plus and Pro subscribers, can drive the browser to complete tasks such as filling shopping carts or creating project tickets. Optional, user-manageable browser 'memories' carry context across sessions, and OpenAI emphasises that users stay in control.
relevance: Puts a general-purpose agent inside the browser, where it acts on third-party sites with the user's sessions and carries persistent context, which is the setting for the cross-organisation disputes in this theme.
